questions.question: The practice data totals NZD 37000 quoted and NZD 29000 accepted. What does about 78.4% describe?

answers.text: The share of customers who accepted a quote.
answers.feedback: There are no customer or quote counts. This is a ratio of values.

answers.text: The profit margin after all business costs.
answers.feedback: The data contains no costs or profit figures.

answers.text: Accepted value divided by quoted value across the three months.
answers.feedback: 29000 / 37000 is about 78.4%. This is a value ratio, not a job-win count.

answers.text: The next month’s expected acceptance rate.
answers.feedback: The small historical dataset does not establish a reliable forecast.

questions.feedback: 29000 / 37000 is about 78.4%. This is a value ratio, not a job-win count.

questions.question: A Free learner hits an upload limit during the CSV exercise. What should they do?

answers.text: Paste the fictional rows as text or check the sums manually.
answers.feedback: The alternative practises the same review skill without an upload.

answers.text: Upgrade immediately to complete this free course.
answers.feedback: A paid plan is not needed for the core practice. Use the supplied alternative.

answers.text: Upload a real client spreadsheet instead.
answers.feedback: Changing the data does not resolve the limit and introduces information risk.

answers.text: Treat the failed upload as proof that the figures are wrong.
answers.feedback: A tool-access limit says nothing about the arithmetic in the data.

questions.feedback: The alternative practises the same review skill without an upload.

questions.question: Which description of current project file limits matches the lesson?

answers.text: Every plan allows the same number of files.
answers.feedback: Current per-project limits differ by plan.

answers.text: Free allows 5 files per project, and upload allowances are separate.
answers.feedback: Project capacity and the upload rate limit are different constraints.

answers.text: A project’s file capacity guarantees unlimited daily uploads.
answers.feedback: You can have space in a project and still reach an upload allowance.

answers.text: Only Enterprise can create a project.
answers.feedback: Projects are available more broadly, subject to plan and workspace availability.

questions.feedback: Project capacity and the upload rate limit are different constraints.

questions.question: Select all suitable actions before connecting a work app.

answers.text: Check that your organisation approves the connection.
answers.feedback: Installation and workplace approval are separate.

answers.text: Review requested permissions and the connected account.
answers.feedback: Permissions and account choice determine what the app can access.

answers.text: Assume every supported action will always ask for approval.
answers.feedback: Approval behaviour depends on the app, settings, and workspace rules.

answers.text: Check important results against the original source file.
answers.feedback: Connected information can still be summarised inaccurately.

questions.feedback: Installation and workplace approval are separate. Permissions and account choice determine what the app can access. Connected information can still be summarised inaccurately.

questions.question: Match each feature with a suitable beginner use.
questions.feedback: Use the feature that fits your task. Availability can differ; a text alternative still lets you practise review.
